coordinates.locator: Piano di Emergenza Esterna INFN-LNGS, ed. 2024 rev. 7, pp. 27-28 (A24 chainage of the laboratory's doors) and the A24 tunnel line of OSM way 24389234 (src:geo-lngs-osm-tunnel-relation): midpoint of the doors' stretch, 6142 m from the Assergi portal (km 117,653); same point as geometry:lngs-hall-c
coordinates.note: Approximate, about ±400 m (derived, not surveyed): the laboratory's entrance (km 124,150) and exit (km 123,440) doors are published as motorway chainage; subtracting the Assergi portal chainage (km 117,653) puts them 6497 m and 5787 m along the tunnel, and the midpoint of that ~700 m stretch is taken as the underground complex. The tunnel line's own length (10 187 m) agrees with the external emergency plan's chainage (10 176 m). Hall C's own position within the stretch, and the order of Halls A, B and C along it, are not published, so all three halls share this point. It replaces the Assergi street-address point (42.4189343, 13.5183438), which is the surface office complex 6.1 km away. It is labelled campus-grade and approximate, as for the other detector sites placed from a building or tunnel position rather than a published hall survey; the source is a prefecture emergency plan, not a survey.
coordinates.quote: L’ingresso ai laboratori si trova al km 124,150, quello di uscita al km 123,440.

depth.note: Average rock coverage of the underground laboratory as a whole (same figure used for Hall B).
depth.quote: The 1400 metre-rock thickness above the Laboratory represents a natural coverage that provides a cosmic ray flux reduction by one million times

depth_mwe.note: Laboratory-wide average overburden, the same for all three halls here: the halls are about 80 m apart and "could feature slightly different rock coverage" (Borexino 2012, Sec. 3). Pandola 2011 gives 3100 m w.e. as the minimum depth and 3800 m w.e. as the average; Mei & Hime 2006 Table I derive equivalent flat-overburden depths of 2.96 to 3.1 km.w.e. from three Gran Sasso flux measurements.
depth_mwe.quote: Borexino is an organic liquid scintillator detector situated at the LNGS, covered by a limestone overburden of 3800 m w.e.

muon_flux.locator: Abstract and Sec. 3; Table 1 (Hall C), JCAP 02 (2019) 046 (arXiv:1808.04207)
muon_flux.note: Borexino sits in Hall C (Table 1 of the paper). The detector identifies muons passing through a spherical volume of 146 m^2 cross section, so its efficiency is virtually independent of the muon incidence angle; mean muon rate 4329.1 ± 1.3 per day. The earlier four-year Borexino value was (3.41 ± 0.01) × 10^-4 m^-2 s^-1 (arXiv:1202.6403). The quote's factor 10^-4 multiplies the bracket, so the stored value is 3.432 × 10^-4 m^-2 s^-1 = 0.0003432 m^-2 s^-1 with no unit conversion.
muon_flux.quote: We have measured the flux of cosmic muons in the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso at 3800 m w.e. to be (3.432 ± 0.003) · 10−4 m−2 s−1 based on ten years of Borexino data acquired between May 2007 and May 2017.

name: LNGS Hall C
notes: No official LNGS page consulted names which specific experiments occupy Hall C individually (only the collective three-hall description is given); that attribution is therefore omitted rather than guessed.

summary.plain: One of three big rooms carved out of the rock under the Gran Sasso mountain in Italy, about 100 metres long.
summary.technical: Underground experimental hall of LNGS, about 100 × 20 × 18 m under ~1400 m of rock, one of the laboratory's three main halls (A, B, C).
